newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn falls, July hits 3-month low on funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn falls, July hits 3-month low on funds.

text.p: CBOT corn futures crumbled and the July contract hit a three-month low on fund selling tied to technical weakness and ideas rapid corn plantings would lead to a bumper crop this fall, traders said.

"First of all the markets are being dictated by weather," said Joel Karlin, vice president of commodities for Chicago-based brokerage house Everen Securities. "The crop is getting in the ground fast and historically, crops yield better when they're planted early."
USDA on Monday said 88 percent of the U.S. corn crop was seeded as of Sunday, ahead of average pace of 67 percent.
Funds sold at least 30 million bushels on the day, keying off of a technical break below $2.80 per bushel in the July. The July traded as low as $2.76, the lowest since February 18.
"It was primarily a fund selling expedition tied to the weak close in the May and the negative charts," said Jack Scoville, analyst with Price Futures.
Floor sources said volume was thin ahead of the midday expiration of the May contracts. When those contracts went off the board weaker, massive selling interest surfaced.
Corn ended 8-1/4 to 4-1/4 cents per bushel lower with July down 8-1/4 at $2.76-1/4.
Some floor sources said farmer selling picked up on the break which contributed to the declines.
"You've got huge fund selling, farmers are starting to sell old crop corn and there's no business going on," one floor source said.

Commercials were light sellers of corn which supported ideas of farmer selling. Continental Grain sold one million bushels July, Term Commodities sold one million September and FCC sold one million December.

Funds sold at least 30 million bushels on the day, led by Rosenthal Collins. Traders said Rosenthal sold at least 10 million bushels July. Merrill Lynch sold four million July while Prudential Securities and Dean Witter each sold 2.5 million July, pit sources said.

In options trade, CIS bought 400 December $2.70 calls at 14-1/2 cents, sold 400 December $3.20 calls at 4-1/2 cents and sold 800 December $2.30 puts at 3-1/4 cents. LFG bought 500 December $2.50 puts at 10 cents.
Corn volume was estimated by CBOT at 57,000 contracts, above Monday's actual volume of 42,558 contracts.
